annotation.title_clean: Council of Europe Framework Convention on Artificial Intelligence and Human Rights, Democracy and the Rule of Law
annotation.title_en: Council of Europe Framework Convention on Artificial Intelligence and Human Rights, Democracy and the Rule of Law
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Council of Europe (published in the Official Journal of the European Union)
annotation.venue: Official Journal of the European Union (2026/1081)
named_instruments_referenced: Council of Europe Framework Convention on AI
annotation.summary_en: Full text of the Council of Europe Framework Convention on AI, signed in Vilnius on 5 September 2024 and published in the EU Official Journal in 2026. It is a binding treaty requiring Parties to align the AI lifecycle with human rights, democracy and the rule of law. It sets principles, remedies, risk management, and a follow-up mechanism.
key_provisions_or_claims: Parties must adopt measures ensuring AI lifecycle activities are consistent with human rights, democracy and rule of law.
Principles: dignity, transparency, accountability, equality and non-discrimination, privacy, reliability and safe innovation.
Remedies, procedural safeguards, and notification when interacting with AI.
Graduated risk and impact management, including assessing moratoria or bans.
Excludes national defence; national security and R&D carve-outs; Conference of the Parties and independent oversight mechanisms.
